children: Strategy Inc. is back at the Bitcoin buffet. After a three-week hiatus, Michael Saylor's firm scooped up 950 BTC worth approximately $75.7 million between September 14 and September 20, marking the company's first purchase since its last buy on August 31.

The average acquisition price came in at $79,670 per coin, including fees. That's a meaningful premium to the company's overall average cost basis of roughly $75,416 per BTC, but still well below Bitcoin's market price of around $85K at the time of reporting.

With this latest purchase, Strategy's total stash has climbed to 846,000 BTC. The firm has spent approximately $63.8 billion accumulating that position over the years, making it far and away the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin on the planet.
At Bitcoin's recent trading price near $85K, the entire position carries a market value of roughly $72 billion. That leaves Strategy sitting on unrealized gains of approximately $8 billion.
The company also disclosed holding $1.05 billion in USD cash reserves, with total USD reserves of $5.04 billion.
The Bitcoin purchase wasn't the only capital allocation move Strategy made during the week. The firm simultaneously repurchased $174 million worth of its STRC perpetual preferred shares.

Saylor, never one to let a purchase go unannounced, posted on social media with characteristic brevity: "A little more orange." MSTR shares jumped roughly 7% in premarket trading following the disclosure, tracking Bitcoin's own move above $85K.

The three-week gap between purchases was notable for a company that has, at various points, been buying Bitcoin on a near-weekly cadence. Strategy's last acquisition before this one came on August 31.

Strategy's average cost basis of $75,416 across all 846,000 BTC means the company needs Bitcoin to stay above roughly $75K to remain in the green on a cost basis. With the asset trading more than $10K above that threshold, the margin of safety is comfortable.

title: Strategy purchases $76M in Bitcoin for first time in three weeks
